doc: A .cld written before the flow properties: read and saved without an edit, it is byte-identical (FR-029).

steps.expect:
causal-loop 1

# Why an on-call rotation gets worse on its own.
#
# Written for this repository, from the pattern any engineer who has carried a
# pager will recognise. Every loop here is labelled correctly; the reference
# example beside this one is where a deliberately wrong label lives.

variable incidents "Incidents"
variable onCallLoad "On-call load"
variable fatigue "Fatigue"
variable mistakes "Mistakes"
variable attrition "Attrition"
variable teamSize "Team size"
variable automation "Automation work"
variable toil "Manual toil"

# ---- the spiral --------------------------------------------------------------
# Incidents wake people up, tired people make mistakes, mistakes cause
# incidents. Nothing in this path is negative, so it compounds.

link incidents -> onCallLoad + weight=1
link onCallLoad -> fatigue +
link fatigue -> mistakes + weight=1.5 "the tired-hands effect"
link mistakes -> incidents +

loop R1 "Tired hands make more work" incidents onCallLoad fatigue mistakes

# ---- the drain ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Fatigue also costs people, and a smaller team carries more each. The delay is
# the point: nobody quits the week they get tired, so the load rises long
# before the cause is visible in a headcount report.

link fatigue -> attrition + delayed "people leave months later, not days"
link attrition -> teamSize -
link teamSize -> onCallLoad -

loop R2 "Fewer hands, heavier rota" onCallLoad fatigue attrition teamSize

# ---- the exit that closes behind you -----------------------------------------
# The obvious reading of this path is "automation is the way out, if only there
# were time" - a balancing loop being starved. The arithmetic says otherwise,
# and the arithmetic is right.
#
# Two negative links, and two is even: load falls automation, automation falls
# toil, toil raises load. That is REINFORCING. The exit does not merely fail to
# open - the busier the team gets, the faster it closes.
#
# This label was originally written as B3 and ADP reported the disagreement.
# The tool was right and the author was wrong, which is the case Requirement 3.3
# exists for.

link toil -> onCallLoad +
link automation -> toil - delayed
link onCallLoad -> automation - "no time to fix the thing that has no time"

loop R3 "Too busy to stop being busy" onCallLoad automation toil
